hypotheses.justification: The theorem takes this as an argument because it is an instance-implicit variable whose type mentions only E. It follows from the other hypotheses: Mathlib's `FiniteDimensional.complete` (Mathlib/Topology/Algebra/Module/FiniteDimension.lean) gives `CompleteSpace E` for a finite-dimensional space over a complete nontrivially normed field. Here the field is ℂ (complete) and E is a normed group (so Hausdorff) with a normed ℂ-module structure coming from `InnerProductSpace ℂ E`, so its conditions hold, and `[FiniteDimensional ℂ E]` is already assumed. To prove the theorem without it, add `haveI := FiniteDimensional.complete ℂ E` at the start; the rest of the proof, including the call to `integrable_jointRep_restrict_prod`, is unchanged. Degenerate cases do not matter because the instance is reconstructed in every case.
